text:
zoe: quick thought — for flaky mobile clients can we do a "slim resume" token that only encodes a tiny offset + checksum so the edge can resume a streaming response without holding heavy state? :thinking:

andrew: +1 on small token, but main worry is side effects. if the request triggered an action upstream, resuming could re-run it. we need idempotency boundary.

chris: agree. simplest model: token -> persistent request id + small lease. resume only allowed if lease still active. otherwise treat as new request or fallback.

maria: feels right. maybe add a lightweight header to indicate client intent: "Resume-Intent: exactly_once|at_least_once" so server can reject resumes for exactly_once flows.

zoe: sketch of token header I had in mind:

```
Resume-Token: v1|req=8a3f|offs=1024|ck=ab12
Resume-Intent: at_least_once
```

sam: how big can tokens be? mobile NATs and proxies will cookie-limit. we must keep them tiny (<128B). also can't keep huge per-client maps at the edge.

infra-bot: note: current lease service default TTL=60s, max entries per-edge=100k. storage and eviction are a factor.

andrew: fallback behavior: if resume-token miss -> either full reconnect + hedging, or respond with `409 Resume-Expired` and instruct client to retry idempotently. Prefer graceful fallback.

chris: tradeoffs: longer leases => more resume hits but more memory. shorter leases => more misses and hedging cost. maybe adaptive: keep longer leases for sessions with high resume-hit probability.

maria: propose heuristic: keep soft-lease for first 30s of stream always; extend if client frequently reconnects (exponential backoff sample). Also differentiate by tenant (paid tiers get longer leases).

zoe: another angle — streaming backpressure: if upstream is overloaded we should let resume attempts get a `103 Early-Resume` with a suggested backoff window instead of hard failing. avoids expensive hedging storms.

sam: is `103` custom? browsers understand 103. we can also use `Retry-After` header on a 409/429. but a lightweight `103` with metadata is neat.

andrew: example exchange idea:

```
> client: POST /v1/generate  (Connection: keep-alive)
< edge: 200 + stream chunks (w/ Resume-Token header on every trailer)
--- client disconnects ---
> client: POST /v1/generate (Resume-Token: v1|req=8a3f|offs=1024)
< edge: 103 Early-Resume; Backoff: 1.5s
< edge: 200 + resumed stream (or 409 Resume-Expired)
```

chris: implementation at the edge: maintain an LRU mapping from `token_hash` -> {req_id, last_offset, created_at, lease_expiry}. On resume request check checksum and lease. If miss, return 409. If hit, replay from offset using cached KV of partial response or re-stream from upstream with `start_offset` param.

maria: caveat: caching partial responses increases storage and complexity. maybe only cache metadata and rely on upstream to support ranged resume. that would push complexity to model-serving.

zoe: good point. we should define two modes: "edge-resume-with-cache" (faster, more state) and "upstream-range-resume" (stateless at edge but requires model support).

sam: metrics we need: `resume_attempts`, `resume_hits`, `resume_misses`, `resume_invalid_checksum`, `resume_latency`, `resume_fallbacks_by_tenant`. also track memory pressure signals to drive eviction.

infra-bot: reminder: any TTL/eviction param needs feature-flag rollout and observability hooks. creating canary config is suggested.

andrew: security: tokens must be HMAC'd with per-tenant key to avoid tampering. include version tag so we can rotate signing scheme.

chris: edge-case: partial side-effects (webhook ack) — if resume occurs after webhook fired, dedupe must be handled upstream. document clearly.

maria: operational plan: 1) RFC for token format + intent header, 2) prototype LRU metadata store + 103 path on a single edge region, 3) add metrics and feature flag, 4) canary with low traffic tenants.

zoe: i'll open an RFC PR with token format & eviction heuristics today. cc @andrew @chris @maria @sam. thanks for quick feedback :thumbsup:

sam: lgtm. small nit — call the header `Resume-Intent` or `X-Resume-Intent`? prefer standard name without `X-` unless needed.

andrew: agree, `Resume-Intent` is fine. let's keep header naming consistent with existing `Intent` headers.

zoe: noted. follow-up RFC will include example curl and small test plan.

chris: add a short test harness that simulates connection churn and measures hit/miss tradeoffs.

maria: good. also include cost model: memory cost vs upstream hedging cost per 1k sessions.

zoe: cool — wrapping up. will paste RFC link here once posted.

infra-bot: scheduled maintenance notice: edge-lease service upgrades tomorrow 02:00 UTC — may affect TTL behavior for brief period.

andrew: thanks, noted.

zoe: thanks all.
